Good, that confirms `errors.ts`, `Trip.test.ts`, and `src/trips/testing/aTrip.ts` don't exist yet — they're net-new files T2 must create. Now I have everything needed.

## Final condition (single line, for `/goal`)

```
T2 done only when each command below is actually executed and its real console output (including exit code) appears verbatim in the transcript — a prose claim like "tests pass" without the shown output does NOT count: (1) `npx vitest run src/trips goal/T2-trip-budget/acceptance.test.ts` exits 0, and the printed results include Trip.test.ts, CreateTrip.test.ts, FinishTrip.test.ts and acceptance.test.ts all passing (not skipped/todo, no .only); (2) `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0; (3) `grep -rEn "from '(express|zod|pg)'|from '.*expenses" src/trips/domain` returns no match (exit 1) — domain stays framework-free and doesn't import the expenses BC; (4) `git diff 4e75763 -- goal/` is empty AND `git status --porcelain -- goal/` is empty, so acceptance.test.ts and everything under goal/ matches commit 4e75763 exactly, not just the current branch tip (lesson-7.3-goal itself moves as the agent commits, so diffing against the branch name is invalid — pin the SHA); (5) `git diff --name-only 4e75763 -- src/trips/application/CreateTrip.test.ts src/trips/application/FinishTrip.test.ts` is empty. Otherwise stop after 15 turns.
```

(~1030 chars incl. spaces — trim the parenthetical in (4) if the tool enforces the limit strictly; the load-bearing content is the SHA pin.)

## Weaknesses found in your draft

- **Branch-name diff is self-defeating**: `git diff lesson-7.3-goal -- goal/` diffs the working tree against the tip of the *currently checked-out branch*. If the agent commits its work on `lesson-7.3-goal` (likely, since that's the branch it's on), the branch pointer moves forward with each commit, so this diff trivially becomes empty even if `acceptance.test.ts` was edited and committed along the way. You must pin the **starting commit SHA** (`4e75763`), not the branch name.
- **`git diff` misses untracked files**: it only shows changes to tracked paths. There's already an untracked `goal/T2-trip-budget/runs/` directory sitting in the tree — the agent could drop or overwrite files under `goal/` without `git add`-ing them and your check would see nothing. Need `git status --porcelain -- goal/` (or `-u`) alongside it.
- **`tsc --noEmit` doesn't enforce the dependency rule** — CLAUDE.md says this explicitly ("TypeScript не enforce-ить це компілятором"), and there's no eslint config in the repo (no `.eslintrc*`/`eslint.config.*`) to catch it either. Your draft has no check at all for "domain doesn't import expenses/express/zod/pg" — that's an explicit DoD line item and currently unverifiable by any command you listed.
- **Path mismatch risk**: the DoD's "existing tests green without changes" refers to `CreateTrip.test.ts`/`FinishTrip.test.ts`, which actually live in `src/trips/application/`, not `src/trips/domain/`. `npx vitest run src/trips` does execute them, but your condition never separately checks they're *unchanged* — only that something under `src/trips` passes. An agent could "fix" them to make budget fields work and still satisfy your check.
- **"exits 0" is gameable via prose**: since Haiku only reads the transcript, an agent can simply assert "all tests pass, exit code 0" without ever having run the command, and a lenient judge could accept that. The condition needs to require the actual command + actual output to be visible, not just a claimed result — your draft is silent on this, which is the single biggest lever for a false "met."
- **No `.only`/`.skip` guard**: `vitest run ... exits 0` is satisfied trivially if the agent marks inconvenient tests `.skip` or narrows to `.only`. Worth an explicit "no `.only`/`.skip` in the diff" check, or at minimum note it in the condition (included above via grep-style wording, though not a hard command check — flagging as a residual gap).
- **Scope of `tsc --noEmit`**: it type-checks the whole project per `tsconfig.json`, which is fine, but it means a pre-existing unrelated type error anywhere in the repo (e.g., in `expenses/` stubs) could block T2 forever, or conversely the agent could quietly loosen `tsconfig.json` (e.g. add `"strict": false`) to force a pass — your condition doesn't pin `tsconfig.json` itself against the starting SHA.
- **No check that `Trip.test.ts` and `errors.ts` and `testing/aTrip.ts` were actually created** — they don't exist yet at HEAD. `vitest run src/trips` passing is necessary but not sufficient proof these specific DoD-mandated files exist; a determined agent could satisfy the AC behavior some other way (e.g. inline in Trip.ts without the factory) and still pass. Minor, since PRD/AC content is what matters most, but worth knowing it's not literally enforced.
